newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Northam union members vote for strike - NUM.
newsitem.headline: Northam union members vote for strike - NUM.

text.p: The National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Wednesday 96.8 percent of its 3,300 members at Northam Platinum Ltd had voted in favour of strike action over wages.
"The majority, 96.8 percent, of our members want to go on strike," NUM regional coordinator Mahlakeng Mahlakeng told Reuters by telephone from Rustenburg.
The union and Northam owners Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd reached deadlock on wage negotiations on September 26.
The remaining 2,200 non-union workers have already acccepted a 10 percent wage increase.
Mahlakeng said the result of the two-day strike ballot would be conveyed to Northam management who would have 48 hours to come up with a revised offer.
Mahlakeng said although the union had initially demanded a 15 percent pay hike, it was prepared to accept 10 percent.
"The actual focal point is the parity," he said, adding that Northam's minimum wage of around 556 rand was well below that of other mines.
He said union members at Northam were prepared to go on strike.
"If we are forced to, certainly we will go on strike and our members are ready. The situation on the ground is that our members feel strongly that Northam is not prepared to bargain with us fairly".
The mine produced 75,365 ounces of precious metals in concentrates in the three months to September.
Northam recorded a net loss before capital spending of 7.39 million rand in the September quarter after turning in a profit of 8.17 million in the previous quarter.
Analysts said the mine would be hard pressed to deal with a strike by almost 66 percent of its workforce.
